newsitem.title: USA: Blast temporarily shuts Oxy Cao Limn production.
newsitem.headline: Blast temporarily shuts Oxy Cao Limn production.

text.p: The second bomb blast in a week on the crude pipeline carrying Colombian Cao Limn crude oil has caused Occidental Petroleum Corp to temporarily shut in output at the Cao Limn field, the company said.

"Because of the second incident involving the pipeline we have been forced to temporarily suspend production pending repairs to the pipeline," a spokesman at Occidental's Los Angeles headquarters said.
Occidental, operator of the Cao Limn field which has daily production of 215,000 barrels, said repairs to the pipeline take anywhere from 24 to 36 hours.
"In the past such repairs to the pipeline have taken a day or a day-and-a-half," the Occidental spokesman said.
Colombia's state-owned Ecopetrol is operator of the damaged pipeline, which carries 200,000 barrels per day of crude the Cao Limon field in northeast Arauca province to the Caribbean port of Covenas.
Ecopetrol spokesmen have said the latest attack on the line occurred early Tuesday, just as pumping operations were set to resume following another attack Sunday.
In all, the pipeline has been blown up 34 times so far this year.
All of the attacks are thought to be the work of National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels, who dynamited the pipeline 47 times last year and spilled more than 105,000 barrels of crude.
